issues.description: Console warning: container has non-static position warning from a scroll offset calculation library (likely react-scroll or similar). Not visible to user but indicates a layout/CSS configuration issue.
issues.root_cause: A scroll-offset library (e.g., react-scroll, framer-motion scroll, or a custom hook) is referencing a parent container that has 'position: static' (the default). The library requires 'position: relative', 'fixed', or 'absolute' on that container to correctly compute scroll offsets.

issues.description: Double page:mount event fired (ts difference is 1ms apart — ts:1776404240784 and ts:1776404240785). Suggests the auth page component is mounted twice, possibly due to React StrictMode double-invocation in development or a duplicate analytics call.
issues.root_cause: In React 18 StrictMode, effects fire twice in development. If the page:mount tracking event is fired inside a useEffect without proper cleanup or inside the component body directly, it will fire twice. Alternatively, the component is rendered in two places in the tree.

fixes.reason: Adding the empty dependency array ensures the page:mount event fires only once on initial mount, not on every render. This prevents the duplicate event log entries observed in the console.
Adding 'position: relative' to the auth container resolves the console warning about scroll offset calculation requiring a non-static positioned container.
